answer: Interleaved Arrival Scheduling: each identity must submit its registration traffic in a scheduled slot chained to a random prior slot, verified against a public relic of past arrivals. New identities sit out a fixed horizon before their first slot, and slot spacing widens inside a crowded grove of pending registrations. An attacker running N parallel sybils must hold each slot open across the full horizon, paying latency and idle connection cost per identity.
